title: The smallest job worth splitting
hints: Try work = 1, 2, 3 and so on, and stop at the first one where `work + n * copy < n * work`.
A recursive helper works: `let rec go w = if w + n * copy < n * w then w else go (w + 1) in go 1`.
Without a loop: the inequality means `(n - 1) * work > n * copy`, so the answer is `n * copy / (n - 1) + 1`.
explain: n devices win when work / n + copy < work. Multiplying by n keeps everything whole: work + n * copy < n * work, which is (n - 1) * work > n * copy. The smallest whole work that passes is n * copy / (n - 1) rounded down, plus 1. For two devices that is 2 * copy + 1: half the work has to be more than the copy time.
